A: So, let’s talk about the results from Chinese Taipei in the World Baseball Classic. They really had a rollercoaster of a tournament, didn’t they?

B: Oh, absolutely! I mean, they started off kind of rough with a couple of shutout losses, but then they pulled it together, right? I think they had a crucial win against Korea!

A: Exactly! They edged out Korea 5-4 in extra innings, which was super intense. Did you catch that game?

B: I did! It was wild. That home run by Yu Chang in the second inning really set the tone. The crowd at the Tokyo Dome was going nuts!

A: Totally! And then they had that back-and-forth battle, like when Tsung-Che Cheng hit that solo shot to put them back in the lead. It’s moments like that that make baseball so thrilling.

B: Right? And then Korea answered back with that towering two-run homer from Do Yeong Kim. I thought, “Oh man, here we go again!” 

A: I know, right? It felt like a heavyweight fight. But what I found fascinating was Ruei-Yang Gu Lin’s performance. He was dealing, only allowing two hits and one run before he got pulled. 

B: Yeah, he really stepped up. I mean, working into the fifth inning with just 59 pitches? That's impressive! 

A: And don’t forget about Wei-En Lin coming in for relief. He struck out four batters! That’s some clutch pitching under pressure.

B: Definitely! It was like the team found their groove at the right moment. And that eighth inning—wow! Stuart Fairchild’s two-run homer was just… chef's kiss, you know?

A: Oh, for sure! And it was such a pivotal moment. You could feel the momentum shift right there. 

B: Exactly! And the fact that they had to wait for the results of the other matches to see if they could advance? Talk about nail-biting!

A: I can only imagine the tension. So, did they make it to the quarterfinals?

B: Well, they were waiting to see how Australia did against Japan and Korea, but they needed those results to fall in their favor. It was like a game of musical chairs with only a few seats left!

A: Ha! I love that analogy. It really captures the suspense of it all. 

B: Right? And I mean, Chinese Taipei really showed resilience. After those first losses, they could’ve easily given up, but they fought back.

A: Exactly! It just goes to show how unpredictable and exciting the WBC can be. 

B: For sure! Can't wait to see how they perform next time. Hopefully, they'll have even more surprises in store!

SOURCE TITLE: 2026 World Baseball Classic: Chinese Taipei Defeats Korea 5-4 in ...
SOURCE CONTENT: Chinese Taipei threw a wrench into Pool C of the World Baseball Classic on Sunday afternoon, edging Korea 5-4 in ten innings behind a strong start from Ruei-Yang Gu Lin and timely hitting.
Following two shutout losses to open the tournament, Chinese Taipei rebounded with two crucial wins and must await the results of Australia vs. Japan and Australia vs. Korea to determine whether they can advance to the quarterfinals via a second-place tiebreaker.
With Chinese Taipei’s win, Japan officially clinched a spot in the quarterfinals. Korea will face Australia tomorrow night. Australia controls its own destiny, but if it loses to Japan tonight, Korea’s hopes will remain alive. In that case, Korea would need a win to potentially advance through a tiebreaker.
Yu Chang opened the scoring with a solo home run off Hyun Jin Ryu in the second inning, igniting the packed Taiwanese crowd at the Tokyo Dome.
Korea chased Gu Lin from the game in the fifth and tied it when Shay Whitcomb bounced into a double play that brought home Hyun Min Ahn.
Tsung-Che Cheng put Chinese Taipei back in front in the sixth with a solo shot, but Do Yeong Kim answered with a towering two-run home run to left field off Wei-En Lin to give Korea its first lead of the day.
Gu Lin pitched admirably for Chinese Taipei, allowing just two hits and one run while working into the fifth inning on 59 pitches. Lin then added 2 ⅓ innings in relief, striking out four while allowing two runs.
Ryu went three innings for Korea, throwing 50 pitches and allowing one run on three hits with three strikeouts. Gwak Been followed with 3 ⅓ innings, giving up one run on two hits while striking out three.
In the seventh, Chinese Taipei put the tying run on second and the go-ahead run on first, but Dane Dunning entered and immediately induced a double play to end the threat.
With two outs in the eighth, the game flipped again when Stuart Fairchild hit an opposite-field two-run homer off Dunning to give Chinese Taipei a 4-3 lead.
